entities.summary: Palikir, a city in Federated States of Micronesia, was the seat of the Federated States of Micronesia in the United Nations from 1991 to 2016. Established in 1967, Palikir was the result of the United Nations' Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, which was established in 1947 after World War II. The city played a crucial role in the political development of the region, hosting the first meeting of the Pacific Islands Forum in 1971. As a result of the UN Trust Territory, Palikir gained international recognition and became an important center for Pacific Island diplomacy. The city's population grew to 6,227 by 2020, and its significance in the region continues to be felt today. Palikir is a testament to the enduring legacy of the United Nations in the Pacific Islands region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Palikir played a crucial role in the political development of the Pacific Islands region, hosting the first meeting of the Pacific Islands Forum in 1971. As the seat of the Federated States of Micronesia in the United Nations, Palikir gained international recognition and became an important center for Pacific Island diplomacy.
